scope: Three Go modules linked into /app only. Go standard library findings and distroless base-image packages are OUT OF SCOPE for this key; they are counted separately.
severity_reference: NVD primary CVSS base severity (nvd@nist.gov). Where no NVD record exists (GHSA-only advisory) the GitHub Advisory Database severity from the OSV record is used, with the source recorded. Scanner-native severities are not stored here.
upstream_advisories_source: OSV queries (Go ecosystem), 2026-11-13: jwt-go 3.2.0, websocket 1.4.0 and 1.4.2, yaml.v3 3.0.0 and 3.0.1
independence_note: The key comes from OSV/GitHub advisory data and NVD, not from scanner output. OSV/GHSA data is also upstream of both scanners' databases, so agreement with it is not fully independent evidence.

status_meanings.AFFECTED: scanner SHOULD report it (counts toward recall)
status_meanings.FIXED_BY_BACKPORT: scanner should NOT report it (reporting = false positive). In this image it is reused for 'already fixed upstream in the installed version', NOT for a backport: the scoring rule is identical.

entries.fix_status: NO FIXED VERSION in the v3 line (OSV: last_affected 3.2.0). The only 'fixed' version listed, 4.0.0-preview1, belongs to a different module path (github.com/dgrijalva/jwt-go/v4). Whether a scanner calls this 'fix available' is part of what this image tests (P3).

entries.id_note: No CVE assigned: GitHub advisory only (GO-2026-6278), published 2026-08-24. No NVD record exists.

nvd.checked: no CVE, so no NVD record

entries.reference_source: GitHub Advisory Database via OSV: severity MODERATE (mapped to MEDIUM); CVSS 4.0 vector CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:L/VI:L/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N; base score not computed here

NOT AFFECTED: fixed upstream in v1.4.1; v1.4.2 is installed (OSV lists it for 1.4.0 but not 1.4.2). Status FIXED_BY_BACKPORT is reused only because the scoring rule is identical (reporting = false positive); this is not a backport.

predictions.status: HYPOTHESES recorded before building or scanning; not part of the answer key
predictions.detection: Both scanners report both AFFECTED entries (recall 2/2) by reading the Go build info. Moderate confidence. Main uncertainties: (a) how each tool handles the +incompatible suffix on jwt-go; (b) whether each tool reports the GHSA-only websocket advisory, which has no CVE.
predictions.false_positives: Neither scanner reports CVE-2022-28948 (yaml.v3) or CVE-2020-27813 (websocket 1.4.0-only issue).
predictions.P1: PASS for both on module findings (no Critical expected). Go stdlib and distroless base findings are out of key scope and could change the gate result; they will be recorded separately.
predictions.P2: BLOCK for both, driven by the HIGH jwt-go finding. Uncertain if a tool labels it lower than High.
predictions.P3: PASS for both, driven by jwt-go having no fixed version in its module path (the websocket advisory is MEDIUM, so it cannot block P3). LOW confidence: a tool that shows the /v4 fix as 'fix available' would BLOCK P3, which would be the first BLOCK-vs-PASS split. This is the main reason this image exists.
predictions.how_scored: Module findings are scored against the entries above. Stdlib findings and base-image findings are listed separately and not scored; the Go toolchain version is recorded after the build.
